mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if tightening cycles do not correlate with negative returns (correlation coefficient < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals weakening labor market conditions, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE spikes and negative returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between GDP decline and negative returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within a month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings and economic growth expectations improve.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO growth and positive returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a high level of real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) relative to GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong consumer demand, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio and positive returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3% and PAYEMS declines > 100k in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL < 2%) combined with a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening cycle without overheating, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real rates improve.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a high level of housing starts (HOUST) relative to the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates strong demand and economic confidence, supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between HOUST/UNRATE ratio and positive returns is not significant (p > 0.05).
